# Bridge publish fails on rejected refs: a GitHub 500 is misread as a stolen lease

## Premise correction (read first)

The original report described the witness failure as "a stale `--force-with-lease`
expectation". **The raw run log disproves that.** It was never a stale lease — it was a
GitHub **server-side error** that rebar's CAS classifier mistook for lease movement.

## Evidence

### Fault 1 — witness publication (run 31455622724, 2026-08-11T03:30Z)

```
WARNING rebar_reconciler._ref_lock: ref-lock: push to origin refs/reconciler/last-pass
  (expected oid 22cd71bd...) classified as CAS mismatch (lease moved) —
  stderr: remote: fatal error in commit_refs
 ! [remote rejected] 1e5caeb7... -> refs/reconciler/last-pass (failure)
WARNING rebar_reconciler._ref_lock: ref-lock: git push to origin refs/reconciler/last-pass
  failed (exit 1) — fail-closed: remote: Internal Server Error
ERROR: cannot publish reconciler last-pass witness: Command '[... --force-with-lease ...]'
```

Attempt 1 was `remote: fatal error in commit_refs` + `! [remote rejected] ... (failure)`.
`_is_cas_mismatch_stderr` in `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py` matched the
broad `rejected` marker, found nothing in `_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS`, and therefore
reported **"classified as CAS mismatch (lease moved)"** — a false claim that another
process stole the lease. Attempt 2 returned `Internal Server Error`, which *is* in the
marker list, so it correctly fell through to fail-closed and killed the pass.

This is exactly the failure shape bug 4afc's subtractive classifier exists to prevent;
the marker list simply does not know GitHub's `fatal error in commit_refs` or the bare
`(failure)` ref-status. Misclassification is not cosmetic: a "stolen lease" verdict is a
statement about **concurrency** that operators use to reason about racing passes.

### Fault 2 — tickets-branch delivery (run 31244501098, 2026-08-08T06:41Z)

```
final-push-rejected: To https://github.com/navapbc/rebar
 ! [remote rejected] HEAD -> tickets (cannot lock ref 'refs/heads/tickets':
   is at e45f61a9... but expected 9ecaaa40...)
 (6 unpushed commits on origin/tickets..HEAD)
```

This one **is** a genuine lost CAS race, and it *was* retried — `cannot lock ref` is
correctly classified retriable, so the loop spent its budget. It still lost every time,
because `src/rebar/_store/push.py` has **no backoff anywhere**: the retries fire
back-to-back and keep colliding with the same concurrent `tickets` writer. Under the
continuous-loop cadence this contention is routine.

## Plan

1. In `_ref_lock.py`, extend `_NON_CAS_REJECT_MARKERS` with the observed server-side
   failure signatures (`fatal error in commit_refs`, and the generic `(failure)`
   ref-status) so a server fault can no longer be reported as lease movement. Keep the
   subtractive shape and the fail-closed default: `stale info` stays conclusive for a
   genuine lease move, and ambiguity still fails closed.
2. In `push.py`, spend backoff between non-fast-forward / CAS retries, reusing the
   injectable backoff seam added for `subzero-locustal-junebug` (this change stacks on
   it), so a lost `cannot lock ref` race gets a real chance to converge instead of
   re-colliding immediately.

**Constraint that shapes step 1:** `_ref_lock.py` sits at exactly the repo's 800-LOC hard
cap, so the markers are appended in a single `+=` statement (with the tuple annotated
`tuple[str, ...]`) rather than added inline with a comment block. The file stays at the
cap. A proper split of that module along a call-graph seam is owed but is deliberately NOT
bundled into this bug fix — it is a refactor with its own risk profile (the reconciler
loads siblings through a custom loader, and existing tests bind to module identity and
logger names).

## Deliberate non-change (and why)

The ticket also asks "whether the last-pass witness failure should be fatal at all (it is
a witness, not the payload)". **This change does NOT downgrade it.** Witness fatality is
the fail-loud contract described in `docs/adr/0094-reconciler-last-pass-two-witness-status.md`,
and the heartbeat canary is the downstream detector that depends on it; relaxing it is a
user-visible alerting change, not a reliability fix, and belongs in its own ticket with an
ADR amendment. This change fixes the **mechanism** that produced the failure (a
misclassified server error, and unbacked-off retries) while leaving the contract intact.

## Scope / non-goals

- No change to `_is_cas_mismatch_stderr`'s subtractive shape, to the `stale info`
  conclusive marker, or to the fail-closed default.
- No change to `finalize_process`'s return contract in `last_pass.py`.
- No change to the CAS retry COUNT anywhere (`_MAX_RETRIES = 5`; the witness's 3 attempts).
- No new secrets, credentials, permissions, or infrastructure.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] AC1: A test proves the exact run-31455622724 stderr (`remote: fatal error in
  commit_refs` with `! [remote rejected] ... (failure)`) is **not** classified as a CAS
  mismatch, i.e. it is no longer reported as a stolen lease.
- [x] AC2: A test proves a genuine lease move (`stale info`) is **still** classified as a
  CAS mismatch — the bug 4afc contract is not weakened by the new markers.
- [x] AC3: A test proves the existing non-CAS markers (`hook declined`,
  `internal server error`, `rate limit`, `file exists`) still classify as non-CAS.
- [x] AC7: `_ref_lock.py` stays within the 800-LOC hard cap (the module-size gate is
  green), and the complexity ratchet reports no new debt.
- [x] AC4: A test proves a `cannot lock ref … is at X but expected Y` rejection sleeps
  between retry attempts (via the injected sleep seam) rather than retrying back-to-back,
  and that the number of push attempts is unchanged.
- [x] AC5: The existing ref-lock classification suite
  (`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_ref_lock_push_classification.py`) and the push
  contract suite pass unchanged.
- [x] AC6: `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass.
